### `Type`

<a id="Type.apply"></a>
#### Type.apply

`Type Type.apply(Type type)`

Returns the result `Type` of a function `Type`, following pointer and array

<a id="Type.base_type"></a>
#### Type.base_type

`Type Type.base_type(Type type)`

Returns the suffix of `type` beginning at its builtin or typedef base.
The result shares the original `List` and is `NULL` when no base is

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.body"></a>
#### Type.body

`List Type.body(Type t)`

Returns the stored body portion of an enum, struct, or union `Type`.
Tag references and `Type`s without a stored body return `NULL`.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.canonicalize"></a>
#### Type.canonicalize

`Type Type.canonicalize(Type type)`

Removes non-typedef storage classes, `inline`, type qualifiers, and
unqualified-value projections from `type`, retaining typedef identity.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.declared"></a>
#### Type.declared

`Type Type.declared(Type type)`

Returns the stored declaration `Type` after removing non-typedef storage
classes and `inline`. Those specifiers describe declaration placement;
`const`, `restrict`, and `volatile` describe the stored value and remain.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.dereference"></a>
#### Type.dereference

`Type Type.dereference(Type type)`

Removes one outer pointer-like or array modifier, or returns `NULL`.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.discards_qualifiers"></a>
#### Type.discards_qualifiers

`int Type.discards_qualifiers(Type source, Type target)`

Returns whether handing a `source` value to a `target` declaration would
silently drop a qualifier the target does not keep. The leading
qualifiers of each type describe the copied value, not what it points
at, so only the deeper levels are compared. Callers use this where the
two types are otherwise the same, or where one points at `void`, which
has no deeper levels to compare; a conversion through a converter
function copies instead of aliasing.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.function_parts"></a>
#### Type.function_parts

`int Type.function_parts(Type type, List &params, Type &?return_type)`

Splits a direct or pointer function `type` into its fixed `params`,
which are `NULL` for `(void)`, and its `return_type` when one is asked
for. Returns 0 and leaves both unchanged when `type` is not a function.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.integer_literal_magnitude"></a>
#### Type.integer_literal_magnitude

`int Type.integer_literal_magnitude( Type type, String text, unsigned long long &value)`

Reads an integer literal of `type` spelled in digits, with any suffix,
into `value`. Returns 0 for any other literal.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.numeric_literal"></a>
#### Type.numeric_literal

`Type Type.numeric_literal(String text, int floating)`

Returns the native type selected by a validated numeric token.
`floating` selects floating suffix rules; an integer outside all supported
native families returns `NULL`. A signed data token includes its sign
when selecting a family, so a signed minimum fits that family.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.numeric_literal_value"></a>
#### Type.numeric_literal_value

`Var Type.numeric_literal_value(Type type, String text)`

Reads a validated numeric literal at its semantic type's precision.
Returns `void` when its magnitude exceeds the integer representation.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.promote"></a>
#### Type.promote

`Type Type.promote(Type type)`

Applies integer promotion to `type`.
Enums and narrow integers become `int`; other scalars retain their
canonical spelling, and a non-scalar returns `NULL`.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.qualify"></a>

`Type Type.qualify(Type type, Type source)`

Source: `lib/type.x`

`Type Type.reference(Type type)`

<a id="Type.rest_container"></a>
#### Type.rest_container

`Type Type.rest_container(Type type)`

Returns the container Type, `("List")` or `("Map")`, that a rest
parameter packs its arguments into, or NULL for any other parameter.
`List @name` has the Type `(.... "List")` and `Map @name` has
`(.... "Map")`.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.rest_index"></a>
#### Type.rest_index

`int Type.rest_index(Type type)`

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.scalar"></a>
#### Type.scalar

`Type Type.scalar(Type t)`

Returns the normalized builtin scalar spelling, or `NULL` when `t` is not

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.scalar_tag"></a>
#### Type.scalar_tag

`Symbol Type.scalar_tag(Type type)`

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.tag"></a>
#### Type.tag

`List Type.tag(Type type)`

Returns the one-element tag `List` of an enum, struct, or union `Type`.
For a compiler-generated anonymous tag, that element is a gensym node. A

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.var_numeric_extractor"></a>
#### Type.var_numeric_extractor

`String Type.var_numeric_extractor(Type type)`

Returns the numeric `Var` reader for `type`, or `NULL` when unsupported.

Source: `lib/type.x`

<a id="Type.var_numeric_update_helper"></a>

`String Type.var_numeric_update_helper(Type type)`

## Runtime-internal callables

These callables connect runtime translation units. They are documented
for source readers but are not supported as user API.

| Function | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`Macro.declaration`](#Macro.declaration) | Constructs a declaration, moving the base type's modifiers to each binding. |
| [`Type.declaration_base`](#Type.declaration_base) | Returns the declaration specifiers `t` without the pointer, array, or function modifiers an alias in them contributes, and sets `modifiers` to those modifiers for `declarator_append_modifiers` to append. |

### `Macro`

<a id="Macro.declaration"></a>
#### Macro.declaration

`List Macro.declaration(Type specifiers, List rows)`

Constructs a declaration, moving the base type's modifiers to each binding.

Source: `lib/type.x`

### `Type`

<a id="Type.declaration_base"></a>
#### Type.declaration_base

`List Type.declaration_base(Type t, List &modifiers)`

Returns the declaration specifiers `t` without the pointer, array, or
function modifiers an alias in them contributes, and sets `modifiers`
to those modifiers for `declarator_append_modifiers` to append.
Storage and source specifier text, such as `("_Noreturn")`, stay on
the base.

Source: `lib/type.x`

## Design notes

These operations inspect captured types without compiler state. Name
resolution and translation-unit registrations belong to the compiler.
